questionText: A control system in which the output is not fed back to influence the input is called:
explanation: An open-loop control system does not use feedback from the output to modify the input.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: For a negative feedback system with forward path transfer function G(s) and feedback transfer function H(s), the closed-loop transfer function is:
explanation: For a standard negative feedback system, the closed-loop transfer function is T(s) = G(s)/(1 + G(s)H(s)).
subject: Control Systems

questionText: The poles of a transfer function are the values of s for which:
optionC: The transfer function is always zero
explanation: The poles of a transfer function are the roots of its denominator polynomial.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: A continuous-time LTI system is asymptotically stable if all poles of its transfer function lie:
optionA: In the right half of the s-plane
optionC: In the left half of the s-plane
explanation: For asymptotic stability of a continuous-time LTI system, all closed-loop poles must have negative real parts and lie in the left half of the s-plane.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: The root locus represents the movement of:
optionA: Zeros of the closed-loop transfer function
optionB: Poles of the closed-loop transfer function as gain varies
explanation: The root locus shows how the closed-loop poles move in the s-plane as a system parameter, usually gain K, varies.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: For a standard second-order system, increasing the damping ratio generally:
optionC: Makes the system unstable in all cases
optionD: Has no effect on the response
explanation: Increasing the damping ratio generally reduces the oscillatory nature and overshoot of a second-order system.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: For a standard second-order system, the damping ratio ζ for critical damping is:
explanation: A second-order system is critically damped when the damping ratio ζ = 1.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: The Routh-Hurwitz criterion is primarily used to determine:
optionC: The frequency of the input signal
explanation: The Routh-Hurwitz criterion determines the number of roots of a characteristic equation in the right half of the s-plane and is used for stability analysis.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: In a Bode magnitude plot, a first-order pole contributes an asymptotic slope of:
explanation: Each first-order pole contributes a slope of -20 dB/decade after its corner frequency.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: For a unity feedback system, the characteristic equation is:
explanation: For unity negative feedback, H(s) = 1, so the characteristic equation is 1 + G(s) = 0.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: A first-order system has the transfer function G(s) = 1/(2s + 1). The time constant, in seconds, is _______.
explanation: Comparing G(s) = 1/(τs + 1), the time constant τ is 2 seconds.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: For a unity feedback system with G(s) = 10, the closed-loop DC gain is _______.
explanation: For unity feedback, T = G/(1 + G) = 10/11 ≈ 0.9091.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: For the characteristic equation s² + 4s + 4 = 0, the damping ratio ζ is _______.
explanation: Comparing with s² + 2ζωn s + ωn² = 0, ωn = 2 and 2ζωn = 4. Thus, ζ = 1.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: A system has closed-loop poles at s = -2 and s = -5. The number of poles in the right half of the s-plane is _______.
explanation: Both poles have negative real parts and lie in the left half of the s-plane. Therefore, there are no right-half-plane poles.
subject: Control Systems

questionText: A first-order system has a time constant of 0.5 seconds. Its pole location is at s = _______.
explanation: For a first-order system G(s) = 1/(τs + 1), the pole is located at s = -1/τ = -1/0.5 = -2.
subject: Control Systems
